title: Command line
summary: This file is the command-line interface, run as `python -m rag ask "question"`. It builds a pipeline with the options you choose (re-ranking, translation, generator), indexes a folder of documents, asks one question and prints the answer, the confidence, the translated query and the citations. It is the quickest way to try the system without starting a server.

key_ideas.explain: When you run `python -m rag`, Python executes `rag/__main__.py`. That gives a package a command-line entry point without installing a separate script.
`add_subparsers` lets one program have several verbs, like `git commit` and `git push`. Here there is one verb, `ask`, which leaves room to add others (for example `ingest`) later.
The CLI re-reads and re-embeds the documents on every run. That is simple and fine for a small corpus, but a large one would save the index with `HybridIndex.save` and load it instead.

blocks.note: Module docstring, written as a usage line: the `ask` command with its options. Line 2 is blank.
`from __future__ import annotations` makes every type hint a lazy string. You can then write `list[str]` or `str | None` on older Pythons (3.8, 3.9) and name a class inside its own body.
`argparse`, the standard library module for parsing command-line arguments.
Imports the generator factory (for `--llm`) and the pipeline. Lines 9 and 10 are blank.
`main` holds all CLI logic, so it can be called from tests or other code without running on import.

L12: the top-level parser, named `rag` in help and error messages.
L13: a subcommand group. `dest="cmd"` stores the chosen subcommand name, and `required=True` makes running `python -m rag` with no command an error with a usage message.

L14: the `ask` subcommand with its help text.
L15: a positional argument, the question. Quote it in the shell: `python -m rag ask "هل عندنا إجازة الأمومة؟"`.

L16: `--docs`, the folder to index, default `data/corpus`, relative to where you run the command.
L17: `--rerank`, a flag (`store_true` means present = True, absent = False) that turns on the cross-encoder.
L18: `--translate`, a flag that also searches with the question translated between Arabic and English.
L19: `--llm`, an optional generator name (`extractive`, `gemini` or `openai`); `None` means "auto-detect from the environment".
L20: `-k`, how many passages to retrieve, parsed as an int, default 5.
Parses `sys.argv` into a namespace object, so options become attributes such as `args.rerank`. Line 22 is blank.

L23: builds the pipeline with the chosen optional stages. This loads e5-small, and the re-ranker if asked.
L24 to L25: if `--llm` was given, replaces the auto-selected generator with the requested one, sharing the pipeline's embedder.

L26: indexes every PDF, TXT and Markdown file in the folder: load, chunk, embed, add to FAISS and BM25.
L27: asks the question and gets an `Answer`.
In the middle confidence band (found but not sure), prints a warning line first, so the reader treats the following text as the closest passage, not a confident answer.

L30: prints the answer text with its `[n]` markers.
L31: prints the confidence kind and value (a cosine or a re-ranker logit) and the generator name. The leading `\n` adds a blank line.
If translation was used, prints the other-language wording, for example `also searched as: Do we have maternity leave?`.
Prints each citation as `[n] chunk_id (page p)`, so you can find the exact passage, for example `[1] employee-handbook.en.md#p1-c3 (page 1)`. Lines 36 and 37 are blank.
The standard guard: `main()` runs only when this file is executed (as `python -m rag`), not when it is imported.
